messages.text: 你好，我想先了解一下這篇論文大概在講什麼？

messages.short_answer: 這篇論文由 Miguel Sicart 撰寫，目的是為「遊戲機制（game mechanics）」提出一個更精確的形式化定義。作者借用物件導向程式設計的概念，把遊戲機制定義為由「代理者（agents）」調用、用來與遊戲狀態互動的「方法（methods）」，並希望藉此連結形式分析、控制器設計與使用者體驗。

sections.title: 論文要解決的問題
sections.text: 作者指出「遊戲機制」一詞在遊戲研究與設計中定義含糊，並以 Gears of War 的掩體機制和極簡遊戲 Orbital 作為開場例子。作者希望提供一個分析工具，用來描述、發現並彼此關聯遊戲中的機制。

sections.title: 核心定義與研究架構
sections.text: 作者將遊戲機制定義為「由代理者調用、為與遊戲狀態互動而設計的方法」，並說明這個定義比以往方法更少以人類為中心，因為人類玩家、AI 或機器人都可以調用機制。論文也區分規則與機制：規則提供可能性空間並規範狀態轉換，機制則是與遊戲狀態互動的方法。

sections.title: 文章結構與應用
sections.text: 論文先回顧既有的遊戲機制定義（如 Avedon、Järvinen、MDA 等），接著提出定義並討論核心機制與主要／次要機制，最後以 Shadow of the Colossus、Rez 與 Every Extend Extra 進行比較分析。作者在結論中承認這個定義仍有缺陷，並留下許多未深入探討的灰色地帶。

sections.title: 說明
sections.text: 簡單來說，這篇論文是在為「遊戲機制」建立一套借自程式設計概念的分析用詞，讓研究者能更系統地描述遊戲如何運作，以及玩家的操作如何對應到輸入裝置與情感體驗。摘要部分依據的是 PaperLens 生成的概覽，細節仍應對照原文確認。

sources.text: The article by Miguel Sicart addresses the ambiguity of the term 'game mechanics' in game research and design, using the cover system in Gears of War and the minimalist game Orbital as opening examples. It proposes a formal definition that treats game mechanics, drawing on object-oriented programming concepts, as methods invoked by agents for interacting with the game state, defined in relation to rules, challenges and emotions used in an instrumental way. The introduction states the aims: to provide an analytical tool for describing game mechanics, to connect formal analysis with controller design and user experience, and to set up a comparative analysis of Shadow of the Colossus, Rez and Every Extend Extra. The pages also outline a plan that includes a review of previous definitions of mechanics, a discussion of primary and secondary mechanics, and a conclusion on the definition's shortcomings, though these later sections are not included in the text shown.

In this article, I propose a definition of game mechanics useful for the analysis of games and their formal constituents. This definition will allow for formalized analysis of game structures, and it will also open up for the possibility of connecting formal game analysis with research on controller designs and user experience. I define game mechanics, using concepts from object-oriented programming, as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state. With this formalized definition, I intend to: Provide a tool to discover, describe, and interrelate game mechanics in any given game. Define mechanics also in relation to elements of the game system, game hardware and player experience, mapping mechanics to input procedures and player emotions. Even though I will be mentioning concepts like game rules, challenges, emotions and user experience, it is not my intention to enter the debate on those topics. Here, I use those concepts in a relational way: defining game mechanics requires mentioning and acknowledging rules, challenges and emotions.
quotes: I define game mechanics, using concepts from object-oriented programming, as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state.

sources.text: These pages define game mechanics as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state, borrowing terminology from object-oriented programming. The author argues this definition is less anthropocentric than prior approaches, since mechanics can be invoked by human players, AI agents, or bots, with examples drawn from Shadow of the Colossus and Gears of War. The text also argues that the framework supports mapping mechanics to input devices, using UML-style modeling, and discusses how fighting-game mastery relates to input mapping. Finally, it introduces 'context mechanics' triggered by the player's situation in the game world, illustrated with Gears of War, Assassin's Creed and Wario Ware, Inc.; the author notes that studying bots' access to mechanics is outside the article's scope.

These pages from Sicart's article 'Defining Game Mechanics' argue for an ontological distinction between rules and mechanics: rules provide the possibility space and regulate state transitions, while mechanics are methods designed for interaction with the game state. The author illustrates this with Shadow of the Colossus, where climbing is a mechanic constrained by a stamina property derived from a rule, and the game loop evaluates interactions against those rules. The text also distinguishes designed gameplay from players' unpredictable uses, such as toyplay, noting that formal design cannot fully determine how a game is played. Finally, it begins an interlude on how qualifiers like core, primary and secondary mechanics fit the proposed definition, drawing on Salen and Zimmerman and Järvinen.

These pages review how game studies has analysed games through their formal elements, distinguishing systems, players, and player-system contexts. They trace the distinction between rules and mechanics from Avedon through Lundgren and Björk, Rouse, Fullerton et al., Cook, the MDA framework, and Järvinen. The authors argue that most prior definitions of game mechanics lack the precision needed for formal analysis, particularly in linking rules to mechanics and identifying individual mechanics. The pages also note that Järvinen's goal-oriented account struggles to explain sandbox play in games such as Sim City and Crackdown.

These pages argue that existing definitions of core mechanics, such as those of Salen and Zimmerman and Järvinen, lack precision because players repeat actions that are not core mechanics (e.g., jumping in FPS games). The author defines core mechanics systemically as game mechanics repeatedly used by agents to achieve a systemically rewarded end state, illustrated with Shadow of the Colossus, Orbital, Sim City and EverQuest. To handle complexity, the paper introduces primary and secondary mechanics, using Grand Theft Auto IV and Gears of War as examples, and notes these categories are analytical aids rather than rigid categories. The pages end by introducing compound game mechanics as sets of related mechanics functioning together within one delimited interaction mode, such as driving.

These pages come from a Game Studies article defining game mechanics, shifting from formal definition to application. The author compares Shadow of the Colossus, Rez and Every Extend Extra through their core input-based mechanics, arguing that each uses a tension-and-release structure. The stabbing mechanic in Shadow of the Colossus, the shoot mechanic in Rez and the explode mechanic in Every Extend Extra are read as design choices that shape intended player experiences such as powerlessness and epic achievement, or synaesthetic musical engagement. The section concludes that developers modified well-known core mechanics to alter player expectations and agency.

These pages conclude Sicart's article defining game mechanics as methods invoked by agents for interacting with the game world, drawing on object-oriented programming and game studies. They discuss practical uses of the definition: formally describing and modifying mechanics, improving game design documentation, and easing communication between designers and programmers. The conclusion argues that mechanics are performative while rules are normative, and that treating them as distinct is useful for analysing computer games. The author acknowledges that the definition is not the ultimate one, that many grey areas remain unexplored, and that no dominant definition of rules or mechanics exists in game studies. The pages end with acknowledgements and a reference list.

Here, I use those concepts in a relational way: defining game mechanics requires mentioning and acknowledging rules, challenges and emotions. I do so in an instrumental way and leave for further research the implications of this definition for understanding other systemic components of games. Since both game researchers and game designers have covered the topic of game mechanics, I begin this article with an analytical summary of the major works on this topic, providing a general overview of these previous definitions of game mechanics and place my work within this tradition. The second part of this article presents the definition of game mechanics, detailing the elements that compose it. I then present a brief reflection on primary and secondary mechanics and how they can be derived from this definition. These concepts are put into practice in the third part, where I perform a comparative analysis of Shadow of the Colossus (Team Ico, 2005), Rez (United Game Artists, 2002), and Every Extend Extra (Q Entertainment, 2006), highlighting the use of this concept of mechanics in the research on game structure and user experience.

sections.title: 定義的原文與各部分含義
sections.text: 作者的定義是：遊戲機制是由代理者調用、為與遊戲狀態互動而設計的方法。作者說明，「方法被代理者調用」這個說法借用自物件導向程式設計，用來形式化描述機制的運作方式。

sections.title: 用簡單的話理解「代理者」與「方法」
sections.text: 可以把代理者想成「做事的一方」，例如玩家操控的角色或遊戲中的 AI 機器人；把方法想成這個角色可以做的「動作」，例如跳躍、射擊。作者的例子是：在《Shadow of the Colossus》中，爬、騎馬、刺擊、跳躍、射箭等都是機制。

sections.title: 代理者不限於人類
sections.text: 作者指出，這個定義不以人類為中心，機制可以由任何代理者調用，包括電腦系統中的 AI 代理者。作者也舉例說，機器人（bots）會專注於一組核心機制來優化互動，這可能影響遊戲的平衡。

sections.title: 機制與規則的區別
sections.text: 作者認為規則提供可能性的空間並規範狀態之間的轉換，而機制則是實際與遊戲狀態互動的部分。作者的說法是：規則是為能動性而建模，機制是對能動性而建模。

In the following section I present a formal definition of game mechanics, together with the arguments that make it a more precise and inclusive approach than those reviewed in this section. Defining Game Mechanics Let's start with a definition: game mechanics are methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state. The different components of this definition require further explanation: "Methods invoked by agents" defines this approach to game mechanics, as it formalizes the use of terminology taken from the object oriented programming paradigm (Weisfeld, 2000). In this appropriation of the terminology, object orientation provides a set of metaphors that describe the elements of systems and their interrelations. I do not want to imply that the analysis of the source code of a game will reveal that all game mechanics have been implemented as methods of classes or that object-oriented programming should be considered a default methodology for the actual production of computer games. Nor am I implying that the Object Oriented Framework should be extended to a formal analysis of all elements of the game.

This design choice may lead to an imbalance in the game system, in terms of its dynamics or its economy. Another extension of this approach would draw a distinction between agents in a game with mechanics and agents without access to mechanics. For example, some bots do have access to mechanics while other game agents do not have access to mechanics and hence cannot interact with the game state. This line of research, however, is outside the scope of this article. The second advantage is that it eases the mapping of mechanics to input devices, allowing for a great degree of granularity in the analysis of games. Applying the conceptual framework of Object Oriented programming determines that an agent invokes a mechanic in order to interact with the game[3]. When it comes to players, input devices - from mouse and keyboard to the Wii Fit Board - mediate this process. In Gears of War, the cover mechanic is invoked by pressing the A button in the controller.

Implicit in this definition is an ontological difference between rules and mechanics. Game mechanics are concerned with the actual interaction with the game state, while rules provide the possibility space where that interaction is possible, regulating as well the transition between states. In this sense, rules are modeled after agency, while mechanics are modeled for agency. In this object oriented framework, rules could be considered general or particular properties of the game system and its agents. All objects in games have properties. These properties are often either rules or determined by rules. These rules are evaluated by a game loop, an algorithm that relates the current state of the game and the properties of the objects with a number of conditions that consequently can modify the game state. For example, the winning condition, the losing condition and the effects of action in the player's avatar health are calculated when running the game loop. This algorithm relates rules with mechanics, exemplifying the applicability of an ontological distinction between rules and mechanics.
quotes: In this sense, rules are modeled after agency, while mechanics are modeled for agency.

messages.text: 所以我的理解是：遊戲機制其實就是遊戲的規則啦，例如「不能跳到牆外面」這種，對吧？那代理者和方法只是把規則換個說法而已嗎？

messages.short_answer: 不完全是。作者認為規則與機制在本體上有區別：規則提供可能的互動空間並規範狀態之間的轉換，機制則是實際與遊戲狀態互動的方法。所以「不能跳到牆外面」比較接近規則，而「跳」這類由玩家調用的動作才比較接近機制。

sections.title: 作者如何區分規則與機制
sections.text: 作者指出，隱含在定義中的是規則與機制之間的本體差異：機制關心與遊戲狀態的實際互動，規則則提供互動得以發生的可能性空間。作者也說，規則是為代理者建模的，機制則是為代理者而建模的。

sections.title: 用邊界與跳躍舉例（非論文原例）
sections.text: 假設遊戲規定「角色不能跳出場地邊界」，這是限定可能性空間的規則。「跳」則是玩家可以調用、用來改變遊戲狀態的動作，屬於機制。這個例子是為了說明區分方式，並非論文中的例子。

sections.title: 「代理者與方法」不只是換個說法
sections.text: 「方法」與「代理者」是作者借用物件導向程式設計的術語來描述機制：機制是可被代理者（玩家或電腦系統）調用的動作。作者在書寫中把機制描述為代理者用來在規則所創造的可能性空間內行動的方式，因此重點在於「誰能調用什麼動作」，而不只是重新稱呼規則。

sections.text: 作者也承認規則與機制的區分仍有許多灰色地帶，並指出有研究者認為機制可以被理解為規則的子集；作者說規則是規範性的，機制則是表演性的。作者同時表示，這篇文章不應被視為遊戲機制的最終定義。

messages.text: 還是不太懂代理者和方法的差別，可以換個方式解釋嗎？我可以理解成「玩家按按鈕」就是方法，那「玩家」就是代理者嗎？

sections.title: 用「玩家-按鍵-動作」的順序來看
sections.text: 作者的說法可以拆成三步：玩家（代理者）想做某件事，透過滑鼠、鍵盤或手把等輸入裝置發出指令，遊戲裡對應的機制（方法）因此被調用，例如掩護（cover）。所以「按 A 鍵」是中介，「掩護」才是方法，而玩家是發動它的代理者。

All of these are methods for agency within the game world, actions the player can take within the space of possibility created by the rules. This definition departs from the implicit anthropocentrism of previous approaches. Game mechanics can be invoked by any 2026/9/5 15:03 Game Studies - Defining Game Mechanics https://gamestudies.org/0802/articles/sicart 5/16 agent, be that human or part of the computer system. For instance, AI agents also have a number of methods available to interact with the gameworld. On occasion, those methods will be other than the ones made available to the human player, which can have consequences worth of analysis. This approach can be particularly interesting when trying to understand the effect of bots in MMORPGs, since bots are agents that optimize their interaction by focusing on a core set of mechanics.

sources.text: A game mechanic, then, is the action invoked by an agent to interact with the game world, as constrained by the game rules. In Gears of War, if the player wants to take cover, she has to press the A button in the controller. This will make the avatar seek cover in the closest environment object that can provide that cover. In that sense, a mechanic is limited by the rules that apply to the gameworld (the general physics simulations, for instance, whose objects are suitable for providing some kind of cover), and, on occasion, to rules that apply exclusively to that particular mechanic - for example, some mechanics can only be invoked in certain environments or gameplay contexts. Following Järvinen (2008), the best way of understanding mechanics as methods is to formalize them as verbs, with other syntactical/structural elements, such as rules, having influence on how those verbs act in the game. For example, in Shadow of the Colossus we find the following mechanics: to climb, ride (the horse), stab, jump, shoot (arrows), whistle, grab, run (and variations like swim or dive).

This design choice may lead to an imbalance in the game system, in terms of its dynamics or its economy. Another extension of this approach would draw a distinction between agents in a game with mechanics and agents without access to mechanics. For example, some bots do have access to mechanics while other game agents do not have access to mechanics and hence cannot interact with the game state. This line of research, however, is outside the scope of this article. The second advantage is that it eases the mapping of mechanics to input devices, allowing for a great degree of granularity in the analysis of games. Applying the conceptual framework of Object Oriented programming determines that an agent invokes a mechanic in order to interact with the game[3]. When it comes to players, input devices - from mouse and keyboard to the Wii Fit Board - mediate this process. In Gears of War, the cover mechanic is invoked by pressing the A button in the controller.

persona_text:
# Persona: Mei

**Who.** Mei is a third-year undergraduate from Taiwan taking a game design course, and a non-native
English speaker. A topic from the lecture caught her interest, so she is reading the teacher's extra
readings on her own.

**What she wants.** To understand the main ideas well enough to explain them and connect them to the
lecture. She has no research project. Reading goal: *Get a general overview of this paper*.

**How she behaves.**
- Writes in Traditional Chinese (繁體字). Interface language: 中文（繁體）.
- Has limited background. Starts with broad questions ("這篇在講什麼？"), then asks for basic definitions.
- Often restates an idea in her own words to check her understanding, and is sometimes wrong (e.g. mixes up
  mechanics and dynamics, or treats a game mechanic as the same thing as a rule or a goal).
- Says plainly when she still does not understand ("還是不太懂", "可以換個方式解釋嗎？").
- Tends to accept answers and rarely opens the sources unless prompted.
- Brings in examples from games she plays or from the lecture and asks whether they fit the paper.

**Papers.** MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research; Game Studies – Defining Game Mechanics.
